newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine GDP rises 3.2 pct in Q2 1996 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Argentine GDP rises 3.2 pct in Q2 1996 - paper.

text.p: Preliminary official figures show Argentina's gross domestic product grew 3.2 percent during the second quarter of the year, against a drop of 4.6 percent in the same period in 1995, the daily La Nacion said Tuesday.

According to the newspaper, the figures were revealed late Monday by the Economy Ministry's Planning Secretary Eugenio Pendas and would signal the first rise in GDP after four negative consecutive quarters.
Pends is quoted as saying that "all indicators are showing growth. Industrial production, energy and natural gas consumption and the level of imports."
Argentina's GDP dropped 3.2 percent in the first quarter of 1996, making growth flat in the first half, against a drop of 1.4 percent in the first half of 1995.

Pends said that if growth continued at its current pace, the second half GDP growth would be around six percent, and if that was to occur, GDP growth for the entire year would stand at about three percent.
Six percent growth in the second half would take Argentine output to the same level of economic activity as in the last six months of 1994, which was a record.
